key_insight: A zero-shot, agentic LLM workflow can extract many lung resection pathology fields from narrative reports without task-specific training, approaching supervised performance.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce manual abstraction burden for cancer staging and tumor registry workflows while improving access to structured pathology data.
method: Built an agentic zero-shot workflow to populate 13 CAP synoptic fields from lung pathology narratives.
Evaluated five open-source generative LLMs and compared them with a supervised GatorTron NER-RE baseline.
Used a registry-aligned evaluation framework to measure extraction quality, including complex relations such as pathologic stage.
evidence_signal: The supervised baseline reached Micro-F1 0.960, while the best zero-shot model (GPT-OSS-20B) reached Micro-F1 0.893 with recall 0.949.
watch_item: Despite strong recall, zero-shot extraction still underperformed the supervised baseline, so deployment would need careful validation before registry or clinical use.
paper_title: Prompt, Plan, Extract: Zero-Shot Agentic LLMs Workflows for Lung Pathology Extraction from Clinical Narratives
